title: Healthcare
tagline: Clinical documentation with AI — discharge summaries, prior-auth letters, policy Q&A — on infrastructure the hospital controls. PHI never leaves the building, so there's no cloud vendor and no BAA in the loop.
scenario: A hospitalist spends 90 minutes a day on documentation. The AI drafts the discharge summary from the chart notes and writes the prior-auth letter citing the plan criteria — the clinician reviews and signs. The bundled Springfield General clinical policy (a clearly fictional sample) is already indexed for Q&A.
steps: Ask the policy a question — the answer cites the exact passages it came from.
Then have Chat draft a prior-auth letter and watch it stream.
Point at the sidebar: “100% local — nothing leaves this device.” That's the whole pitch.

ctas.label: Ask the clinical policy →
ctas.prompt: What must a discharge summary include, and what is the deadline for completing it?

ctas.label: Draft a prior-auth letter →
ctas.prompt: Draft a prior authorization letter for an MRI of the lumbar spine for a fictional patient with 8 weeks of radicular back pain, failed physical therapy and NSAIDs, and progressive foot weakness. Cite typical plan criteria. Mark it DRAFT — FICTIONAL SAMPLE.

why.head: PHI stays on-prem
why.body: no business associate agreement, no cloud data-processing addendum, no per-token metering of patient data.

why.head: Volume economics
why.body: documentation runs all day, every day; flat-cost hardware beats metered tokens at clinical volumes.

why.head: Works in restricted networks
why.body: clinical VLANs and facilities with no external egress are the norm, not the exception.

notes: Stay on documentation and policy work — do not demo reading X-rays or scans with the general vision model; it will answer confidently and wrongly. For imaging, point at the healthcare playbook and NVIDIA's specialized medical-imaging stack instead.
Everything shown is labeled FICTIONAL SAMPLE — say so out loud before a clinical audience; they will ask.
The line that lands: “the one dataset you can never paste into a chatbot is the one this box is built for.”
